title: Ages of Man
heading: Ages of Man
summary: Defines the infant, child and adolescent life stages by age band, and explains that the liminal periods between stages let a player modify the character.
quotes: an infant character is between birth and seven years old, a child character between eight and 14, and an adolescent character between 15 and 21

title: Starting Age for Young Characters
heading: Age
summary: Explains how to choose a young character's starting age, the penalties younger characters suffer, and that starting age also fixes starting experience points.
quotes: Characters younger than 14 have penalties applied to Characteristics and Size

title: Aging Chart (Characteristic and Size Modifiers by Age)
heading: Aging Chart
summary: A table giving, for each age, the Characteristic Modifier applied to every Characteristic and the Size Modifier of a young character.
quotes: apply the Characteristic Modifier to all of the character's Characteristics

title: Characteristics and Size for Young Characters
heading: Characteristics and Size
summary: Young characters allocate Characteristic points like adults, then apply the age-based Characteristic and Size modifiers from the Aging Chart.
quotes: younger characters have 7 points allocated toward Characteristics

title: Virtues and Flaws for Young Characters
heading: Virtues & Flaws
summary: Age does not change how many Virtues and Flaws a character may take; they must balance at child character generation, with an exception for apprentices who already have the Free House Virtue.
quotes: At character generation, the number of Virtues must equal the number of Flaws.
Young grogs can have up to three points of Virtues and Flaws, and young companions and apprentices can have up to ten
related: ArM5 p.37 Virtues and Flaws Rules and Guidelines

title: Changing Social Status
heading: Changing Social Status
summary: Sidebar on how a child's Social Status Virtue or Flaw changes during play, and that the change does not require re-balancing other Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: In such cases, simply change the Social Status Virtue or Flaw.

title: Social Status for Young Characters
heading: Social Status Virtues & Flaws
summary: A child normally takes the Social Status of the parent as Son or Daughter of that status; children without a recognized parent are bastards or orphans, and apprentices take the Apprentice status.
quotes: Every character needs a Social Status Virtue or Flaw.

title: Virtues That Grant Experience Points (and Skilled/Weak Parens)
heading: Virtues That Grant Experience Points
summary: Experience-granting Virtues are barred for young characters, and Skilled Parens and Weak Parens are given concrete Teaching Source Quality and Lab Total values within a standard apprenticeship.
quotes: a Skilled Parens must generate a Teaching Source Quality of 18, or have a combined Communication + Teaching of 9, and needs a highest applicable Lab Total of 50

title: Virtues and Flaws That Affect Size
heading: Virtues & Flaws That Affect Size
summary: How Size-altering Virtues and Flaws apply as a child grows, including how smaller characters stay stunted and when they advance a Size step.
quotes: A normal baby grows to Size 0 by age 14

title: Inherited Virtues and Flaws
heading: Inherited Virtues & Flaws
summary: A new type of Virtue or Flaw that is paid for at creation but only manifests later, by player choice or in response to play; it must appear by adulthood.
quotes: All Inherited Virtues and Flaws must materialize by adulthood (age 21).

title: Child Virtues and Flaws
heading: Child Virtues & Flaws
summary: A new type of Virtue and Flaw reflecting childhood boons and banes; they must be exchanged for another of like value during a Transition of Maturation.
quotes: you must exchange the Child Virtue or Flaw for another Virtue or Flaw of like value (Minor for Minor, Major for Major)

title: Abilities for Young Characters
heading: Abilities
summary: Covers yearly experience points for Abilities by starting age, vocational Abilities limited by the parent's score, Supernatural Abilities for Gifted children, the mid-career apprentice experience model, and age limits on Ability scores.
quotes: After 5 years of age, the character gains 15 experience points a year.
The child character's score is limited to half the parent's vocational Ability score during these years.
The character receives 19 experience points per year of apprenticeship for the first 12 years
related: ArM5 p.31 Ability caps by age
ArM5 p.32 spells at character generation

title: Example Childhoods
heading: Example Childhoods
summary: Sidebar of ready-made Ability packages for the experience points a character has accumulated by age five, to speed up character creation.
quotes: The following Ability packages describe how to spend the 45 experience points a character has accumulated by age 5

title: Optional Rule: Abilities for Infants
heading: Optional Rule: Abilities for Infants
summary: Optional rule for characters aged five or younger giving yearly experience points, a fixed part of which must go to a Living Language and the rest to a short list of Abilities.
quotes: he receives 24 experience points per year

title: More Powerful than Normal
heading: More Powerful than Normal
summary: Sidebar warning that young Gifted characters advanced season by season can outstrip stock magi, and advising the standard study model to keep power level equal.
quotes: limit them to the standard study model
related: ArM5 p.33 Extremely Complex Character Generation

title: Transitions of Maturation
heading: Transitions of Maturation
summary: At the ages between life stages the player may exchange Virtues and Flaws for ones of equal value, with restrictions on experience-affecting, Size-affecting and background Virtues and Flaws, and Child Virtues and Flaws must be gone by the last transition.
quotes: Both must be exchanged for Virtues and Flaws of equal value: Minor replaced with Minor and Major replaced with Major.

title: A Standard Apprenticeship
heading: A Standard Apprenticeship
summary: A benchmark year-by-year model of a fifteen-year apprenticeship giving the experience points and spell levels an apprentice receives, used to build mid-apprenticeship characters.
quotes: In game terms, the player receives 240 experience points to spend on Abilities and Arts, and 120 levels of spells.
an apprentice gains 19 experience points a year for eleven years of the apprenticeship

title: Childbearing
heading: CHILDBEARING
summary: Resolves whether a birth succeeds by treating the delivering mother as having an imaginary wound with recovery rolls, with the baby losing Fatigue as it worsens; midwives, physicians, relics and Creo Corpus spells can help.
quotes: treat the delivering mother as if she had a Medium Wound
If the baby loses five Fatigue levels, it dies.

title: Birth Apparitions
heading: BIRTH APPARITIONS
summary: Characters with realm-linked Virtues or Flaws may be born with a brief apparition from their realm, whose Might depends on how strong the Virtue or Flaw is; an Aegis of the Hearth may block it.
quotes: Most have a Might Score of 5, if the child has a Minor Supernatural Virtue or Flaw, or 10 for a Major Virtue or Flaw, and rarely have magical powers.

title: Religious Rites for New Babies
heading: RELIGIOUS RITES FOR NEW BABIES
summary: Christian baptism and the equivalent Jewish and Muslim birth rites cancel non-Divine supernatural effects on a child and drive out possessing spirits, without hindering The Gift.
quotes: baptism cancels any supernatural effect not associated with the Divine realm that may be affecting the child at the time of baptism

title: Born with The Gift
heading: Born with The Gift
summary: Discusses whether The Gift is hereditary in a saga, with an adjusted Ease Factor for finding Gifted children if it is, and how Gifted babies relate to the Order.
quotes: reduce the Ease Factor to 6
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.53 Blood Rights

title: Gifted Babies
heading: Gifted Babies
summary: Describes how the social penalties of The Gift affect an infant's relationships, from loving parents to abandonment, as background for a Gifted child character.
quotes: The negative social influence of The Gift permeates every relationship in life, both intimate and incidental.

title: The Gift Revealed
heading: The Gift Revealed
summary: Explains that The Gift can show itself at birth, at puberty or after a trauma, and that its social consequences begin as soon as it emerges.
quotes: Sometimes it is evident at birth, other times it is triggered by puberty or an early traumatic event.

title: Turbulence
heading: Turbulence
summary: Introduces Turbulences, uncontrolled magical outbursts from a Gifted child's emotional distress.
quotes: Hermetic magi refer to these displays as **Turbulences**

title: Incurring a Turbulence
heading: Incurring a Turbulence
summary: When a Gifted child botches a stressful activity involving magic, a roll against the storyguide's stress die, and also against the character's age, determines whether a Turbulence occurs.
quotes: To see if a character incurs a Turbulence the player rolls the character's Intelligence + a stress die + Aura against the storyguide's roll of a stress die (no botch).
INCURRING A TURBULENCE: Intelligence + stress die + Aura vs. Higher of stress die (no botch) and character's age

title: Controlling Turbulences
heading: Controlling Turbulences
summary: A Stamina roll against the character's Warping Score decides whether the child controls a Turbulence; the difference of the two totals, halved, sets the magnitude of the effect.
quotes: CONTROLLING A TURBULENCE: Stamina + stress die vs. Warping Score + stress die
CONTROLLED TURBULENCE MAGNITUDE: Stamina + stress die total – Warping Score + stress die total/2
UNCONTROLLED TURBULENCE MAGNITUDE: Warping Score + stress die total – Stamina + stress die total/2

title: Effects of Turbulence
heading: Effects of Turbulence
summary: Describes what Technique and Form a Turbulence takes, how it interacts with Magic Resistance and Penetration, how a child can deliberately force one by spending a Confidence point, and how Turbulences fade as the child ages.
quotes: TURBULENCE PENETRATION: Penetration Ability times (1 + sympathetic multiplier)
The player must spend a Confidence point, at which point he checks to incur a Turbulence

title: Turbulences and the Aegis of the Hearth
heading: Turbulences and the Aegis of the Hearth
summary: Sidebar on how a covenant's Aegis of the Hearth affects a child's Turbulence depending on whether the child took part in the Aegis ritual, plus the invitation-token debate for apprentices.
quotes: Subtract half the level of the *Aegis of the Hearth* spell from the roll the player makes to incur a Turbulence.

title: Infant Character Design Notes (Wounds)
heading: Character Design Notes
summary: Warns that infant characters are extremely fragile and offers two options for damage: trading wounds for Flaws or adding the age modifier penalty to Wound Recovery rolls.
quotes: The second option is add the child character's age modifier penalty to any wound recovery roll that the character needs to make.
related: Lords of Men p.125 Option: Mitigating Deadly Wounds

title: Growing Up: Training by Parents
heading: Growing Up
summary: Mundane children learn by copying the same-sex parent; grog and companion parents can spend a free season training a child using their Training Source Quality, and covenant upbringing differs from village life.
quotes: A parent spends one of the free seasons training the child, who receives experience points based on the parent's Training Source Quality.

title: Finding an Apprentice
heading: Finding an Apprentice
summary: A magus can spend a season searching for an apprentice with a Perception roll against an Ease Factor, helped by assistants whose own checks lower that Ease Factor.
quotes: The player makes a Perception + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 12 to successfully find an apprentice
The assistant character makes a Characteristic + Ability check against an Ease Factor of 12.
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.17 Bonisagus apprentice rules
Houses of Hermes: Societates p.128 Pralix

title: Detecting the Gift
heading: Detecting the Gift
summary: Sidebar giving the Intellego Vim guideline for detecting The Gift, its limits against the False Gift and Magic Resistance, and the warning that scrying on another magus is forbidden.
quotes: Intellego Vim spells can detect The Gift. The base level is 10

title: Becoming an Apprentice
heading: Becoming an Apprentice
summary: How a found child becomes an apprentice, which Abilities a pre-apprentice child may have, and how an untrained child can help in the laboratory by adding to Safety, Aesthetics and a Mentem Specialty.
quotes: The character adds his Intelligence divided by 2 to a lab's Safety, +1 to Aesthetics, and +1 to a Mentem Specialty

title: Opening the Arts
heading: Opening the Arts
summary: Opening the Arts is a season-long procedure that lets an apprentice cast and legally binds the apprentice to the magus; a parens with a low Art score gives the apprentice a Deficiency, which is a crime.
quotes: A magus should have a score of 5 in all 15 Hermetic Techniques and Forms.

title: Opening Arts with Supernatural Abilities
heading: OPENING ARTS WITH SUPERNATURAL ABILITIES
requires: Apprentice with a Supernatural Virtue or Ability
summary: When a Gifted child has Supernatural Abilities, the parens needs a high enough Intellego Vim Lab Total to Open the Arts; meeting it destroys the Ability, doubling it keeps it, and the Ability can be converted into an Hermetic Virtue.
quotes: the parens' Intellego Vim Lab Total must equal or exceed 5 times the apprentice's score in any non-Hermetic Supernatural Ability
To maintain existing Supernatural Abilities, the Lab Total must double the necessary level.

title: After the Arts Are Opened
heading: AFTER THE ARTS ARE OPENED
summary: Once Opened, an apprentice has score 0 in every Art, can cast spontaneous spells and read casting tablets with the right Abilities, and uses the standard magical formulas with current Arts.
quotes: Once the Arts are Opened, the apprentice character has a 0 in each of the five Techniques and ten Forms.

title: Delaying Opening the Arts
heading: Delaying Opening the Arts
summary: A magus may delay Opening the Arts, but the child is not legally his apprentice until then and other magi may take her; keeping a Gifted lab assistant is a low crime.
quotes: He can declare the child his apprentice, but she isn't legally bound to him until he Opens her Arts.

title: Teaching Schedule
heading: Teaching Schedule
summary: Sidebar explaining the traditional apprenticeship schedule from Bonisagus' letters: score 5 in all Arts before Opening, one teaching season each year, early Latin and Magic Theory study, and a Gauntlet at the end.
quotes: According to the Peripheral Code, a magus must teach his apprentice for one season every year.
Generally, apprentice magi gain scores of Latin 4, Artes Liberales 1 and Magic Theory 3 by the time they reach adolescence.

title: Legal Issues for Apprentices
heading: Legal Issues
summary: Covers the Code of Hermes provisions on apprentices: legal recognition on Opening the Arts, the season of instruction, the apprentice as the parens' property in Wizards' Wars and trades, the parens' liability, no appeal for the apprentice, and fosterage.
quotes: The parens must personally instruct the apprentice for one season during each year of apprenticeship
related: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.17

title: Teaching Hermetic Virtues
heading: Teaching Hermetic Virtues
summary: A Gifted parens trained in Magic Theory can teach an Hermetic Virtue he has in one season by generating a Teaching Source Quality that meets a Target Level, which rises with the student's existing Hermetic Virtues and falls if the teacher includes an Hermetic Flaw.
quotes: TEACHING SOURCE QUALITY: Communication + Teaching + 3 + bonus
THE TARGET LEVEL IS 15 TO LEARN A MINOR HERMETIC VIRTUE
THE TARGET LEVEL IS 21 TO LEARN A MAJOR HERMETIC VIRTUE

title: Acquiring House Virtues
heading: ACQUIRING HOUSE VIRTUES
summary: An apprentice gains the free Minor House Virtue after enough seasons of one-on-one interaction with the parens, while Mystery Cult Houses use an initiation into the Outer Mystery and House Ex Miscellanea gives a package of Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: ACQUIRING THE MINOR HERMETIC HOUSE VIRTUE REQUIRES 10 SEASONS OF ONE-ON-ONE INTERACTION WITH PARENS
related: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.16 Ritual of Twelve Years

title: Gaining Hermetic Flaws
heading: GAINING HERMETIC FLAWS
summary: Hermetic Flaws gained after character generation take effect immediately and are permanent barring a story; common sources are learning Virtues with a Flaw, uncontrolled Temporary Twilight and Deficiencies from Opening the Arts.
quotes: Hermetic Flaws acquired after character generation affect a character as soon as they are gained, their effects manifesting immediately.

title: Teachers (Gifted Students and Mundane Teachers)
heading: TEACHERS
summary: Mundane teachers dislike Gifted students; The Gift's social penalty applies to Teaching Source Quality for a Gifted teacher and to a Gifted student, and the Parma Magica removes it.
quotes: A character with the Gentle Gift is not penalized, and a character with the Blatant Gift suffers a –6 penalty.
related: ArM5 p.75 The Gift social penalty

title: Book Learning for Young Characters
heading: BOOK LEARNING
summary: A young student can study summae and tractatus if he can read and has enough fluency in the book's language, subject to the owner's or covenant's limits on access.
quotes: must be fluent in the language used in the book (a score of 4 or higher in the written language)

title: Training an Apprentice
heading: TRAINING
summary: A magus may train an apprentice in Abilities, not Arts, without needing Teaching, though the Training Source Quality is usually lower; it still counts as a season of one-on-one instruction.
quotes: Only Abilities can be trained, not Arts, but a trainer does not need an additional Ability (Teaching) to train, like a teacher does.

title: Cantations
heading: Cantations
summary: Cantations are low-level formulaic spells taught to child apprentices; an apprentice can learn many in a season, and being formulaic they are cast even when the casting total falls somewhat short of the spell level.
quotes: In a single season, an apprentice can learn a number of spells equal to her parens' highest applicable Lab Total
the spell casting total needs to fall short of the spell level by 10 or more to fail

title: Optional Rule: Learning Cantations in Play
heading: Optional Rule: Learning Cantations in Play
summary: Optional rule letting a player turn a spontaneous spell the character has cast repeatedly in play into a formulaic spell by spending adventure experience points, at a cost based on the spell level.
quotes: He must use the same spell repeatedly, at least as many times as the level of the spell.
The level of the spell determines its cost, at one experience point per level.

title: Supernatural Interests in Adolescents
heading: Supernatural Interests
summary: Describes how Infernal, Divine, Faerie and Magic beings treat adolescents, including a bonus for adolescents invoking a patron saint and the point that magical compulsion toward sin is not itself a sin.
quotes: who receive a +1 bonus to the roll to invoke their patron saint
related: Realms of Power: The Divine p.87

title: Life in the Covenant (Adolescent Characters)
heading: Life in the Covenant
summary: Adolescent characters follow the same two-work, two-free season pattern as their parents, and can take part in adventures, often being chosen for low-risk missions.
quotes: an adolescent character must work two seasons a year

title: Life in the Laboratory (Apprentice as Lab Assistant)
heading: Life in the Laboratory
summary: Rules for an apprentice assisting in the parens' laboratory: adding to the Lab Total, sharing the parens' work schedule, limits on missed days, shared labs, creating and improving spare labs, and low-level solo activities like extracting vis, fixing arcane connections and opening devices.
quotes: Like other laboratory assistants, an apprentice adds his Int + Magic Theory to his parens' Lab Total.
The apprentice can also miss up to 10 days out of the season and not damage the laboratory activity.
related: ArM5 p.103 distractions in the lab
Covenants pp.107-110 laboratory routines and refinements

title: New Laboratory Flaw: Shared Lab
heading: New Laboratory Flaw: Shared Lab
summary: A new laboratory Flaw for a lab too small for several magi working on independent projects at once, with its Quality and Safety penalties.
quotes: **Shared Lab** is a Free Outfitting Flaw.

title: Laboratory Turbulences
heading: LABORATORY TURBULENCES
summary: A young apprentice may have to check for a Turbulence midway through a stressful laboratory season; an uncontrolled one cuts the apprentice's contribution to the Lab Total.
quotes: if it is uncontrolled, reduce the Apprentice's Lab Total aid by half

title: Bellum
heading: Bellum
summary: A game apprentices play by casting Ager Belli to make illusionary soldiers fight, decided by repeated Intelligence plus Finesse rolls judged by a peer, or by forcing the opponent to lose concentration with a second spell.
quotes: Each round, the participants make an Intelligence + Finesse + stress die roll.
Maintaining a spell while casting a second requires a Stamina + Concentration + stress die against an Ease Factor of 15.

title: Failing an Apprentice
heading: Failing an Apprentice
summary: Apprentices fail mainly by losing The Gift, gaining the Failed Apprentice Social Status in place of Apprentice, or by being abandoned by their parens, which is a low crime and leaves the apprentice outside the Order.
quotes: Once The Gift is lost, the character immediately gains the Minor Social Status Virtue: Failed Apprentice
related: Guardians of the Forests p.114 Fenistal

title: Losing the Gift
heading: LOSING THE GIFT
summary: For player characters, losing or suppressing The Gift is the player's choice and never a die roll; for storyguide characters it can be chosen or determined by an optional botch-dice roll after a stressful laboratory season.
quotes: For a player character, losing The Gift is always the player's choice and never decided by a die roll.
roll an additional number of botch dice equal to the parens' Lab Total divided by 10 (round up)

title: Apprenticeship's End: The Gauntlet
heading: Apprenticeship's End: The Gauntlet
summary: The Gauntlet is the parens' test that decides whether an apprentice becomes a magus; it covers who sets it, how long a parens may delay it, how to run it as an adventure, and an optional single roll to pass it.
quotes: Make an Intelligence + Ability + stress die roll against an Ease Factor of 9 for the apprentice character.
OPTIONAL RULE FOR PASSING A GAUNTLET: Apprentice's Intelligence + Appropriate Ability + stress die vs. 9
related: Houses of Hermes: Societates p.83 Tytalus

title: Learning Parma Magica
heading: LEARNING PARMA MAGICA
summary: An apprentice accumulates Parma Magica experience through exposure but cannot invoke it until the final key instruction is given after swearing the Oath of Hermes; teaching it earlier is a High Crime.
quotes: Usually, an apprentice character finishes apprenticeship with a score of 1 in Parma Magica.
doing so before the apprentice swears the Oath of Hermes is a High Crime

title: Post-Apprenticeship
heading: Post-Apprenticeship
summary: What a newly Gauntleted magus does next, customary gifts, and the recommended minimum Ability scores, noting that an apprentice is a magus once Opened, trained and passed.
quotes: The recommended minimum Ability scores for a magus are Artes Liberales 1, Latin 4, Magic Theory 3, and Parma Magica 1

title: Houses of Hermes Gauntlets
heading: Houses of Hermes Gauntlets
summary: Sidebar summarizing the typical Gauntlet of each Hermetic House and how to build a pre-Gauntlet adventure around it.
quotes: An apprentice of House Tremere must face his master in certamen to pass his Gauntlet.

title: Scholae Magicae
heading: Scholae Magicae
summary: Explains why schools for Gifted apprentices rarely work: Gifted children clash without a Parma Magica, Turbulences are common, mundane teachers need protection, and the Arts must be taught one-on-one.
quotes: The Hermetic Arts must be taught one-on-one, from magus to apprentice, and this limitation has yet to be overcome.
related: The Sundered Eagle: The Theban Tribunal p.33
Against the Darkness: The Transylvania Tribunal chapter 6
